methods.label: Use Danielle's age as the common whole
methods.explanation:
The two percentages refer to different people, so first express every age as a percentage of Danielle's age.

Sally is \(100\%-40\%=60\%\) of Danielle's age. Mary is \(100\%+20\%=120\%\) of Sally's age, so Mary is \(1.2\cdot60\%=72\%\) of Danielle's age.

Their combined age is therefore \(100\%+60\%+72\%=232\%\) of Danielle's age. Thus Danielle's age is
\[
23.2\div2.32=10\text{ years}.
\]
Mary is currently \(0.72\cdot10=7.2\) years old. She is between her seventh and eighth birthdays, so she will be \(\boxed{8}\) on her next birthday, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
